newsitem.title: USA: Gonzalez still top Democrat on U.S. House Banking. [CORRECTED 20:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Gonzalez still top Democrat on U.S. House Banking. [CORRECTED 20:55 GMT]

text.p: U.S. Democrats on Wednesday re-elected Rep. Henry Gonzalez of Texas as the party's senior member of the House Banking Committee, approving him by acclamation after his chief challenger, Rep. John LaFalce of New York, stepped aside.

Gonzalez survived despite the contention that at 80 (corrects from 82) he was no longer able to lead the Democratic Party's defense against the Republican majority. However, he said it would be his last two-year term as ranking Democrat on the panel.

LaFalce, who had the support of House Democratic leader, told reporters he had agreed to serve as chief deputy, a "co-equal" as he said Gonzalez described it. LaFalce will also remain the senior Democrat on the Small Business Committee.
The re-election came as a surprise to many, including Rep. Barney Frank, D-Massachusetts, who told reporters before the vote that, "Henry, unfortunately, is not up to the job."

Lawmakers credited Gonzalez with making a well-received, impassioned speech for his re-election, stressing his seniority and his successful leadership of the minority Democrats in the last congressional session. "We were unified and we met every single objective," he said in remarks prepared for delivery before the closed Democratic caucus.

The loss of support by the Democratic leaders clearly angered Gonzalez. "It is wrong, based on the record. And it is unfair," he said. He added, "I will not cower, I cannot retreat, and I will defend myself."
"I appeal to your sense of justice: one last term as ranking member, and I will not disappoint you," he said. LaFalce quipped after the vote, "Henry was so good, I almost voted for him."

On the first ballot, Gonzalez polled 82 votes, LaFalce 62 and Rep. Bruce Vento, D-Minnesota, 47. LaFalce removed himself before the next ballot, saying he had intended to run only if Gonzalez was challenged by another member.
